title: Change Usher recognition and contracts
summary: Change the deterministic Cell membership report, evidence readers, CI gate, packaging, or contracts while preserving the declaration-only boundary.
use_when: Usher code, tests, membership rules, CLI, JSON, packaging, or contracts must change.
do_not_use_when: Only a report or a correction to another product declaration is needed.
outcome: A tested change whose source, contracts, recognition criteria, and CI behavior agree.
effects: Changes product-owned code, tests, docs and packaging, plus the Cell gate when necessary.
Does not run agents or mutate service state as part of recognition.
authority: Usher owns its recognition contract; Cell owns membership policy and products own their declarations.
success: Synthetic false-positive/false-negative tests and the root ./ci.sh pass; documentation states the exact evidence and proof boundaries.
failure_and_recovery: Keep failures visible and fix their source. Do not relax membership rules or hide products to make CI pass.
privacy: Release documentation contains no secrets or live records. Recognition metadata remains caller-owned output.
steps: Read Usher instructions and maintained terminology through Semantics, using Cell while usher registration remains absent.
Implement the smallest change and update exact product contracts and shared operational documentation.
Run the root ./ci.sh, inspect Usher findings, and keep release/deployment separate from development.
checkpoints: Recognition remains a read-only deterministic declaration check.
Global collisions and incomplete inventory evidence remain visible; other relationships and quality remain outside Usher.
adaptation: Add a universal membership condition only through an explicit Cell policy change, not by discovering an implementation dependency.
stop_when: The change would silently claim actual registration, installation, quality, conformance, or another system relationship.
does_not_authorize: Release publication, deployment, or operations on other systems.

consumers.statement: Local contributors may change Usher under Cell product authority.

preconditions.statement: The intended recognition behavior and affected ownership boundaries are explicit.

inputs.statement: Product source, tests, instructions, current contracts, and requested behavior.

outputs.statement: A tested change whose source, contracts, recognition criteria, and CI behavior agree.

data_semantics.statement: Recognition validity describes explicit repository declarations; domain quality and other relationships remain outside the result.

identity_and_units.statement: Product release version and content-addressed release identity are separate from capability contract and JSON schema versions.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: The change is validated against the exact candidate source through Cell CI.

access.statement: Product-owned source and local CI; no direct service database access.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Source changes and their exact contracts are kept together. Root CI rejects source changes during a plan.

operational_limits.statement: Recognition remains entirely code and does not invoke agents, services, shells, or network.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Changed recognition or JSON meaning is explicitly versioned and tested; no silent reinterpretation of prior output.

reliances.statement: Development reads maintained project terminology through the registered Semantics repository while code and contracts remain behavior authority.
